diagnostics.title: State update after await in an effect
diagnostics.message: This setter runs after `await`, so overlapping re-runs of the effect can resolve out of order and write stale state; gate it behind a cancellation/ignore flag or return a cleanup that cancels the work.
diagnostics.help: In a `useEffect` whose dependencies can change, guard any setter call that runs after an `await` behind a cancellation/ignore flag, or return a cleanup that cancels the async work.

diagnostics.title: preventDefault on a form or link
diagnostics.message: Your users can't submit this <form> without JavaScript because onSubmit calls preventDefault(), so use a server action like `<form action={serverAction}>` to make it work either way.
diagnostics.help: Use `<form action>` where your framework supports it (it works without JS), or use a `<button>` instead of an `<a>` with preventDefault.

diagnostics.title: Custom modal instead of dialog
diagnostics.message: Screen reader users get native dialog semantics for free from the HTML `<dialog>` element, so swap this `role="dialog"` element for `<dialog>` and open it with `dialog.show()` (non-modal) or `dialog.showModal()` (modal).
diagnostics.help: Replace the wrapper with `<dialog>` and open it with `dialog.showModal()`. For the trigger, prefer `<button commandfor="id" command="show-modal">` (Chrome 135+), or a `useRef` with `dialogRef.current?.showModal()`.

diagnostics.message: Unused file is not reachable from any entry point, so it adds maintenance surface without shipping any code.
diagnostics.help: Delete the file if it is truly unreachable, or import it from an entry point.

diagnostics.title: Array index used as a key
diagnostics.message: Your users can see & submit the wrong data when this list reorders or filters, so use a stable id like `key={item.id}`, not the array index "index".
diagnostics.help: Use a stable id from the item, like `key={item.id}` or `key={item.slug}`. Index keys break when the list reorders or filters.

diagnostics.title: Chained array iterations
diagnostics.message: This loops over your list twice because .map().filter() makes two passes, so do it in one pass with .reduce() or a for...of loop
diagnostics.help: Combine `.map().filter()` style chains into one pass with `.reduce()` or a `for...of` loop, so you only loop over the list once
